libc_deps: arm-none-eabi-nm -u on the Cortex-M4 objects (BUILD.txt). y.tab.o: malloc, memset (mal), strchr (yylex metachar test), free + memcpy (bison yyparse stack relocation beyond YYINITDEPTH=200), exit + vfprintf + fputs + fputc + _impure_ptr (fatal), printf + putchar (printre only). compile.o: mal, fatal, printf (printprog only). sub.o: mal, memmove (gcc turned update()'s pointer-copy loop into memmove). pike.o: mal, memset, gen, newsub/incref/update/decref. backtrack.o: memset, fatal, newsub/incref/update/decref. recursive.o: fatal only. thompson.o: mal, memset, gen. Net for an engine port: malloc (never freed), memset, memcpy/memmove, strchr, plus a fatal() replacement. No setjmp, no strlen, no memcmp.
ram_model: malloc everywhere through mal() (malloc+memset), nothing is ever freed. Per pattern: AST Regexp nodes 20 B each on ARM32 (+4 nodes = 80 B for the implicit '.*?' prefix and group-0 wrapper), Prog 8 B + 24 B per Inst (Inst carries a 'gen' field used as a GLOBAL visited mark by pike/thompson, so a Prog is not shareable between concurrent matches). Captures: Sub = 88 B (ref, nsub, 20 pointers) allocated on demand and recycled through the global free list 'freesub' (never returned to malloc). Per pikevm() call: 2 thread lists of 4+8*prog->len B malloc'd and LEAKED every call. yyparse: 1248 B stack frame (bison YYINITDEPTH=200 x (4 B value + 2 B state)), grows via malloc/free/memcpy up to YYMAXDEPTH 10000. Stack (-fstack-usage, Cortex-M4 -Os): backtrack() 12048 B frame (Thread ready[1000] x 12 B; fatal('backtrack overflow') when 1000 pending threads are exceeded, e.g. '(a*)*b' on 37 a's + c); recursive()/recursiveloop() 24 B per frame with one frame per VM step -> depth is unbounded (proportional to input length x program), no guard; pikevm 64 B + addthread 64 B per recursion level (depth <= program length); yyparse 1248 B. Fixed limits: MAXSUB=20 pointers -> groups 1..9 usable; pike/backtrack Save/update() write sub[2n],sub[2n+1] with NO bounds check -> heap overflow for patterns with >=10 groups (the recursive variants do check pc->n >= nsubp). Globals (bss): 36 B (bison yychar/yylval/yynerrs, input, parsed_regexp, nparen, gen, compile pc, freesub). Not reentrant (static parser state, global gen, global freesub).
features_verified: From parse.y/compile.c/executors (not the README). yylex treats exactly the bytes | * + ? ( ) : . as metacharacters (strchr("|*+?():.")); EVERY other byte is a literal, including \ [ ] ^ $ { }. Implemented: literal bytes; '.' = any byte except NUL (so it matches '\n' and one byte of a UTF-8 sequence); alternation '|'; concatenation; '*' '+' '?' greedy and lazy ('*?' '+?' '??', via reg->n=1 and swapping Split targets in emit); capturing groups '(...)' numbered 1..9 (MAXSUB=20); non-capturing '(?:...)'; unanchored search via a prepended lazy '.*?' and group 0 added in parse(); Perl leftmost-first priority semantics (pike/backtrack/recursive). NOT implemented: anchors ^ $, all backslash escapes (\d \w \s \b \. ...), bracket classes, {n,m}, case-insensitive matching, UTF-8 awareness, any way to write a literal metachar, empty pattern / empty alternative / empty group (grammar requires at least one 'single' per branch -> 'syntax error'), '.' excluding newline. Errors go through fatal() -> exit(2); compile() cannot return failure. Executors: recursive (unbounded C recursion, correct results on the corpus), recursiveloop (BUG: its 'Any' case has no NUL check, so '.*?' runs past the end of the string: 'z' on 'abc' printed 'match 395 396'), backtrack (explicit 1000-entry stack, no empty-loop guard), pikevm (Pike VM, refcounted captures, correct on nested empty loops), thompsonvm (no submatch tracking: start is always offset 0; end = leftmost-first end).
difftest: Driver /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-boogie-Workspace-mini-regexp/980e397c-0a6d-407c-9809-54b70c85e624/scratchpad/engines/rsc-re1/driver.c (34 lines, plain cc), one binary per executor (BUILD_driver.txt). No adaptation was needed for search-anywhere or captures: re1's parse() itself prepends '.*?' and wraps group 0. '-i' is answered with 'error' (re1 has no case folding; emulating it by rewriting letters as (?:a|A) was deliberately NOT done). Results on corpus_seed1.jsonl (2088 cases, 7 skipped expect=error, 2081 checked): pike pass 707 fail 1374 timeouts 0 group_spans_checked 45; backtrack pass 705 fail 1376; recursive pass 705 fail 1376; recursiveloop pass 123 fail 1958; thompson (spans only) pass 670 fail 1411. Classification (classify.py, classify_all.txt), pike variant, every failure accounted for: MISSING FEATURE 1114 = backslash escapes \d \w \s \b etc. 687 + -i case-insensitive flag 212 + ^ $ anchors 120 + [...] classes 62 + {n,m} 33; SEMANTICS/GRAMMAR 239 = empty pattern, empty alternative 'a|' '(|a)' or empty group '()' rejected as syntax error; SEMANTICS 21 = byte-wise matching of UTF-8 (11: '.' consumes one byte; 7: a quantifier binds to the last byte of a multi-byte literal, e.g. 'é+' on 'ééé' gives [0,2], 'ő?ű' on 'ű' gives nomatch) + '.' matches newline 2 + '(a*)*' on 'b' leaves group 1 unset ([-1,-1] vs Python [0,0]) 1; BUG 0; TIMEOUT 0. backtrack: same buckets plus BUG 2 ('(a*)+' on 'b' and '((?:.*c*)*yz-)': no empty-loop guard -> loops until MAX=1000 -> 'backtrack overflow' fatal). recursive: same plus BUG 2 (same two cases: unbounded recursion -> segfault, empty output). recursiveloop: 87 failures directly attributable to the read-past-NUL bug and the rest of its buckets are inflated by garbage/crash output (1042 'escapes' etc.). thompson: 31 extra failures 'start always 0' (no submatch). Note 427 corpus cases use none of -i \ [ ^ $ {; pike passes 707 because many 'missing feature' patterns happen to yield the expected nomatch when metachars are read as literals.
caveats: (1) A results file for this label already existed from an earlier agent run (15:14 today); I re-cloned nothing (the clone at engines/rsc-re1/src was present at the expected commit) but re-ran bison, every measure.sh, nm -u, the driver build, difftest and my own classifier; Cortex-M4/M0+ numbers agree with the earlier file, my x86-64 figure (4288) is higher than the earlier 3964 because I keep the yyparse/parse/mal .cold error-path fragments and apportion __cstring by the ARM string sizes -- Mach-O has no per-symbol sizes, so x86 per-function numbers are address differences (nm -n), +-20 B. (2) THE number (2468) is the pike variant; the smallest capture-capable variant is recursive at 2006 B but it has unbounded C recursion and segfaults on '(a*)*'; backtrack (2243) needs a 12 KB stack frame. (3) fatal() (74 B) excluded; add it if error reporting counts. (4) Source not modified; y.tab.c generated with bison 2.3 (Apple's), a different bison version changes yyparse/table sizes. (5) Toolchain: arm-none-eabi-gcc 10.3.1 20210824, Apple clang 21 per measure.sh. (6) The 10+-group heap overflow in pike/backtrack was found by reading update()/Save and not exercised (corpus max is 9 groups). (7) Relevance to the project: re1 is a teaching skeleton -- 2.0-2.5 KB on M4 of which 1.4 KB is a bison parser and it lacks escapes, classes, anchors, {n,m}, -i and UTF-8; it uses malloc and never frees; it demonstrates the compile-to-VM + Pike VM structure (pikevm+addthread = 492 B, sub.c = 126 B) but is not a candidate to embed as-is.
